text.p: These are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Man cleared of trying to defraud bank of millions of dollars. Norman Lowell had been accused of circulating forged $1 million bills of exchange in England. The bills were issued under Banque Generale of Brussels and endorsed by Mid-Med Bank.
- Opposition leader Alfred Sant promises to beef up consumer protection laws. The labour leader says a company should be seen as having a monopoly even with less than 40 percent market share.

- Prime Minister Eddie Fenech Adami visits sister island of Gozo, where he was given an enthusiastic welcome. The paper says Gozitans have already decided to vote for the Nationalist party in the Oct 26 general election.
